The Human in the Loop

We often speak of “automation” as a way to remove human error, but automation usually just relocates the error to a higher level of abstraction. A human might misconfigure a server; an automated script might misconfigure a thousand.

Automation does not eliminate the need for human judgment; it scales the impact of that judgment.

A truly human-centered system provides “guardrails, not walls.” It assumes that an operator will eventually need to take manual control and ensures the interface for doing so is visible, predictable, and calm.
